themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike—suggesting a new or coordinated posting campaign in Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
Statistically significant spike ranked as highest deviation from baseline in district
Concentrated temporal signal suggests acute, not chronic, problem
reporting_angles: Knock on doors in neighborhoods where complaints clustered; photograph and document the illegal postings themselves
Contact 311 and NYC Department of Sanitation to learn if they've identified a pattern (political campaign, commercial advertisement, gang tags) and response timeline

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Street Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 14 this week versus a 4.8-per-week average over 8 weeks—a 195% spike—paired with a simultaneous 967% surge in litter basket requests (4 this week vs. 0.4 avg) and 700% spike in graffiti complaints (6 this week vs. 0.8 avg), indicating a coordinated public realm breakdown this week.
evidence: Sidewalk condition: 14 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.99)
Litter basket requests: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
Graffiti: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.04)
Three simultaneous service categories spiking in same week indicates systemic street maintenance failure, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Walk affected blocks with smartphone; document sidewalk conditions, missing/overflowing litter baskets, and graffiti density to assess if complaints match reality
Interview Sanitation district manager about staffing, scheduling, and recent operational changes; cross-reference with budget requests for maintenance equipment upgrades (recurring CB ask)

themes_detail.label: Trash Collection Crisis Deepening
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints hit 15 two weeks ago (a 500% spike from the 2.5-per-week baseline)—and now intersects with this week's 967% surge in litter basket requests and 195% sidewalk deterioration spike—suggesting trash infrastructure is overwhelmed and visible public health risk is mounting.
evidence: Missed collection: 15 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.9, 500% increase)
Complaints persist with convergence of downstream signals: litter baskets overflowing THIS WEEK (967% spike), sidewalks deteriorating THIS WEEK (195% spike)
Pattern suggests structural failure in waste management, not temporary disruption
reporting_angles: Interview residents on blocks with repeated missed collections; photograph piled bags and overflowing baskets to show accumulation rate and pest risk
Request Sanitation Department records on collection schedules, vehicle breakdowns, staffing absences, and planned service changes for Central Harlem over past 3 weeks

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 8 two weeks ago versus a 0.5-per-week baseline—a 1,500% increase—suggesting either a new unlicensed vending problem or a shift in NYPD/Department of Consumer Affairs enforcement activity in Central Harlem.
evidence: Vendor enforcement: 8 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 8.66, 1,500% increase)
Spike is localized and acute, suggesting policy change or enforcement operation rather than gradual trend
No follow-up data showing whether complaints have normalized or persisted this week
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Consumer Affairs and NYPD to determine if enforcement action targeting street vendors was launched 2–3 weeks ago; request scope and stated rationale
Interview licensed and unlicensed vendors in high-complaint blocks to understand compliance, fines, and operational impact

themes_detail.label: Water Infrastructure Stress Signals
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints jumped to 5 three weeks ago (264% above the 1.4-per-week baseline), and the district has a chronic, recurring budget ask for Department of Environmental Protection capital upgrades—suggesting aging water infrastructure may be flagging system stress.
evidence: Water conservation complaints: 5 THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.65, 264% spike)
DEP capital upgrade is recurring Community Board budget request (signals chronic unmet infrastructure need)
Broader 90-day pattern: 533 water leak complaints + 920 plumbing complaints in district indicates widespread system stress
reporting_angles: Request DEP asset condition assessments for water mains and service lines in Central Harlem; cross-reference against age of infrastructure and recent main breaks
Interview Community Board about what DEP capital projects have been requested repeatedly and why they remain unfunded
